correctness.rationale: For the precisely defined 11-vertex 20-edge graph and threshold-one three-state map, verify_decomposition.py constructs all 177147 transitions, exhaustively eliminates indegree-zero vertices, enumerates directed cycles, then propagates first-entry depths and individual basins. This finite functional-digraph algorithm proves exact global coverage, not sampled simulation. verify_trajectories.py independently reconstructs graph incidences and computes the full orbit, depth and basin spectra by direct trajectory tracing, matching every COUNTS.json cell. verify_irrotational.py independently counts the 13887 extinction states by checking ten fundamental excitation 1-form circulations, using the published equivalence. A digit-encoded witness 1985 enters period four only after nine updates; all 120 depth-nine states go to period four. verify_basecycle.py reproduces the C5 comparison.

value.rationale: The Grötzsch graph is the smallest triangle-free 4-chromatic graph and first nontrivial Mycielski lift of an odd five-cycle. Exact refractory excitation dynamics on this canonical network is a motivated test of how chromatic lift geometry changes sustained wave patterns. Unlike the base five-cycle (only period five and extinction 153/243), the 11-vertex lift supports precisely periods 3,4,7,10 with 1290 nonconstant primitive attractors, 32 distinct individual basin sizes, a sharp nine-step entrance, and extinction probability only 1543/19683. Full exact basin structure is reproducible, useful as a benchmark for graph excitable media and nontrivial beyond a general fixation criterion.
